summary: Browser-only redirect script published as npm package for CDN delivery
details: The package's main file (px.js) is browser-side JavaScript that injects a full-screen iframe pointing to https://mfmz.aliyungood.cn/H.html. It uses DOM APIs (document, iframe) and would throw if required in Node.js. A shipped shell script (update_px8my.sh) automates rotating the destination domain, bumping the package version, republishing to npm, and purging the jsDelivr CDN cache — indicating the package is used as a jsDelivr-hosted browser redirect vehicle rather than a Node library. There are no install/lifecycle scripts, no exfiltration of installer data, no credential access, and no code execution against machines that run `npm install` or `require('px8my')`. The abuse surface is browser end-users who load https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/px8my/px.js in a page, not npm installers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
